Avodah Zarah 71a:1.english: GEMARA: We learned in our Mishna that during wartime, soldiers do not have leisure, and there is no concern that they committed a transgression. And the Gemara raises a contradiction to this from that which is taught in another mishna (Ketubot 27a): With regard to a city that was conquered by an army laying siege, all the women married to priests located in the city are unfit and forbidden to their husbands, due to the concern that they were raped by the soldiers, even though it is wartime! Rav Mari resolved the contradiction and said: They do not have leisure to pour wine for libations, because they are concerned about the war, and the inclination for libation is not strong at that time. But they have leisure to engage in intercourse, because this inclination is strong, even during wartime.

Avodah Zarah 71a:2.english: MISHNA: With regard to Jewish craftsmen (i.e., Israelites) to whom a gentile sent a barrel of wine used for a libation in lieu of their wage (in exchange for their work), and this wine is forbidden for benefit — it is permitted for them to say to him: Give us its monetary value, how much the barrel is worth. But once the barrel has entered into their possession, it is prohibited for them to say so, as that would be tantamount to selling libation wine to the gentile and deriving benefit from its value.

Avodah Zarah 71a:3.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: It is permitted for a person to say to a gentile: Go and placate the collectors of the governmental tax on wine for me, and I will reimburse the gentile subsequently, even if the gentile pays the tax with wine used for a libation.

Avodah Zarah 71a:4.english: One of the Sages raised an objection from a baraita: A person may not say to a gentile: Go in my stead to the commissary [la’otzer] to pay the wine tax for me, if the gentile pays it with wine used for a libation. Rav said to him: Are you saying that the case I am referring to is similar to one who says to a gentile: Go in my stead to the commissary? In that case, since the Jew says: In my stead, whatever the gentile gives the commissary is considered as though the Jew gave it himself. This case that I am referring to is comparable only to that which is taught in the baraita: But the Jew may say to a gentile: Save me from the commissary. For Rav is not speaking of a case where the Jew asks the gentile to enter in his place, but only that the gentile save him.

Avodah Zarah 71a:5.english: MISHNA: In the case of a Jew who sells his wine to a gentile, if he fixed (determined and agreed upon) a price before he measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, deriving benefit from the money paid for the wine is permitted. He is not considered as one who sells wine used for a libation, as the gentile purchased the wine before it became forbidden, and the money already belonged to the Jew. But if the Jew measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, and it already became forbidden, before he fixed a price (before the wine was acquired by the gentile), the money paid for the wine is forbidden, because he became like one who sells wine used for a libation, from which benefit is prohibited.

Avodah Zarah 71a:6.english: GEMARA: Ameimar says: The legal act of acquiring an object by pulling it applies to a gentile. Know that it is so, as those Persians send gifts [pardashnei] to one another and do not retract them, which shows that they acquire one from another by pulling the object alone, even without paying for it. Rav Ashi says: Actually, I will say to you that pulling an object does not acquire it in a transaction involving a gentile, and the fact that they do not retract their gifts is not due to the halakhot of acquisition but because they are taken over by haughtiness, and they consider it shameful to retract a gift.

Avodah Zarah 71a:7.english: Rav Ashi said: From where do I say that acquisition by pulling does not apply to gentiles? It is from that which Rav said to certain wine shopkeepers: When you measure wine for gentiles, take the zuzim from them and then measure the wine for them. And if they do not have zuzim with them readily available, lend them zuzim and then take those zuzim back from them, so that it will be a loan provided to them that they are repaying. As if you do not do so, when it becomes wine used for a libation it becomes so in your possession, and when you take the money it will be payment for wine used for a libation that you are taking. Rav Ashi concludes his proof for his opinion: And if it enters your mind that pulling an object acquires it in a transaction involving a gentile,

Avodah Zarah 71b:1.english: from the moment that he pulled it, the gentile acquired it, whereas it did not become wine used for a libation until he touched it. Therefore, the seller can receive payment for the wine he sold, because at the time of the acquisition the wine was permitted.

Avodah Zarah 71b:10.english: Rava said: Then why, in the second instance, where he paid the money, may he not return it? Is the purchase in the first clause a mistaken transaction but the purchase in the latter clause not a mistaken transaction? Rather, Rava said: The purchase in the first clause and the purchase in the latter clause are both a mistaken transaction, but in the case presented in the first clause, where he did not pay him the zuzim, it does not appear as though there is idol worship in the possession of a Jew, and so he may return it. By contrast, in the latter clause, where he did pay him the zuzim, it appears as though there is idol worship in the possession of a Jew, and therefore he must cast away the object rather than return it.

Avodah Zarah 71b:11.english: The Gemara cites a claim against Rav Ashi’s opinion that a gentile cannot acquire an item by pulling it: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear an objection to your opinion from the mishna: In the case of a Jew who sells his wine to a gentile, if he fixed a price before he measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, deriving benefit from the money paid for the wine is permitted, as the wine was acquired by the gentile before he touched it. And if you say that pulling an item does not acquire it in a transaction involving a gentile, why is the money paid for it permitted? Rav Ashi replied: Here we are dealing with a case where the gentile paid him a zuz in advance, before the measuring, thereby acquiring the wine with money.

Avodah Zarah 71b:12.english: One of the Sages raised an objection: If that is so, say the last clause: But if the Jew measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, thereby rendering it forbidden, before he fixed a price, the money paid for the wine is forbidden. And if he paid him a zuz in advance, why should the money paid for it be forbidden?

Avodah Zarah 71b:13.english: Rav Ashi said to him: And according to you, as you say that pulling acquires items in a transaction involving a gentile, why in the first clause is the money paid for it permitted, and in the latter clause the money paid for it is forbidden?

Avodah Zarah 71b:14.english: Rather, what have you to say to explain the distinction between the two cases? You say that when the Jew fixed a price, the gentile consequently relied on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled, and so the sale was concluded by the pulling. But in a case where the Jew did not fix a price, the gentile did not rely on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled, and therefore the sale was not concluded.

Avodah Zarah 71b:15.english: According to my opinion as well, even though the gentile gave the Jew a zuz in advance, if the Jew fixed a price, the gentile relied on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled, and if the Jew did not fix a price, the gentile did not rely on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled.

Avodah Zarah 71b:16.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear another proof against your opinion, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: A descendant of Noah, i.e., a gentile, is executed by the court for theft of even less than the value of one peruta; but if he stole less than the value of one peruta from a Jew, it is not subject to restitution, i.e., he is not obligated to return it, as the Jew presumably waived the debt. And if you say that pulling an item does not acquire it in a transaction involving a gentile, why should he be executed? He did not commit a legally significant act by stealing the item, as it remains in the possession of the owner.

Avodah Zarah 71b:17.english: The Gemara answers: He is executed because he caused a Jew distress by stealing the item, even though by the halakhot of acquisition the thief did not acquire it.

Avodah Zarah 71b:2.english: The Gemara rejects this proof: If it is a case where the seller measures the wine and pours it into the vessel of a Jew, it is indeed permitted to do so without receiving payment first. Rav’s ruling is not necessary unless the gentile’s vessel is set on the ground, so that there is no act of acquisition before the wine becomes forbidden.

Avodah Zarah 71b:3.english: The Gemara raises an objection: Ultimately, even in this case, when the wine reaches the interior airspace of the gentile’s vessel, he acquires it, as this too is a mode of acquisition. And it does not become wine used for a libation until it reaches the bottom of the vessel, making contact with it, so the acquisition occurs before the wine becomes forbidden. Can one conclude from this that in the opinion of Rav a stream of liquid serves as a connection between two bodies of liquid? If so, when the Jew pours the wine into the gentile’s vessel, the flow of wine that is in contact with the forbidden wine at the bottom of the vessel would render all the wine being poured into the vessel forbidden.

Avodah Zarah 71b:4.english: The Gemara rejects this conclusion: No, a stream of liquid does not serve as a connection, and therefore if the gentile is holding the vessel in his hand, the gentile indeed acquires the wine before it becomes forbidden, and therefore the money paid for it is permitted. Rav’s ruling is not necessary unless the gentile’s vessel is set on the ground, so that there is no act of acquisition before the wine becomes forbidden.

Avodah Zarah 71b:5.english: The Gemara asks: But let the vessels of the gentile acquire the wine from the moment it enters the interior airspace. Can one conclude from this that if the buyer’s vessels are in the domain of the seller, the buyer does not acquire the merchandise once it is placed in his vessels? This is an issue that is subject to a dispute between the Sages, which remains unresolved.

Avodah Zarah 71b:6.english: The Gemara rejects this: No, actually, I could say to you that the buyer acquires the merchandise in such a case. But here, where the wine is rendered forbidden before being acquired by the gentile, we are dealing with a case where there is a remnant of wine remaining on the mouth of the gentile’s jug [kuzanta], which renders the wine poured into the jug forbidden, as each bit of wine becomes libation wine when it comes into contact with the remnant of wine on the mouth as it is poured into the jug. This is why Rav told the wine shopkeepers to take the money before measuring the wine into the gentile’s vessel.

Avodah Zarah 71b:7.english: The Gemara raises an objection: And in accordance with whose opinion does Rav say this? It is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel; as, if it were in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, doesn’t he say that libation wine that became mixed with other wine may all be sold to gentiles for the monetary value of the entire mixture except for the value of the wine used for a libation that is in the mixture? Accordingly, it is permitted to accept payment for wine that was poured into a gentile’s vessel, and the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

Avodah Zarah 71b:8.english: The Gemara answers: The explanation of this ruling can be only according to the opinion of Rav, who issued the ruling. And doesn’t Rav say that the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel only in the case of a barrel of permitted wine that became intermingled with another barrel of libation wine, but not in the case of wine that became mixed with other wine in the same barrel? Therefore, explaining Rav’s statement as contradicting the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is not problematic; consequently, it cannot be proven from his statement that a gentile does not acquire an item by pulling it.

Avodah Zarah 71b:9.english: The Gemara raises another objection to the statement of Ameimar that a gentile can acquire an object by pulling it. It is taught in a baraita: With regard to one who buys broken vessels made of gold or silver from the gentiles and finds among them an object of idol worship, if he pulled the idol worship, thereby performing an act of acquisition, before he gave the zuzim to the gentile, he may return the idol worship to the gentile. But if he pulled it after he gave the zuzim to the gentile, he may not return it. Since the idol’s status was not revoked, he must take it and cast it into the Dead Sea. In that case, if it enters your mind that pulling an object acquires it in a transaction with a gentile, as Ameimar maintains, then why may he return the idol worship once he has pulled it, since it is his? Abaye said: He may return it because it appears to be a mistaken transaction, since he clearly did not intend to purchase idol worship.

Avodah Zarah 72a:1.english: And what does it mean that the stolen object is not subject to restitution? It means that it is not subject to the halakhot of restitution, because it is not technically a theft.

Avodah Zarah 72a:2.english: The Gemara asks: If that is so, say the latter clause of that halakhic statement: If another descendant of Noah came and took the stolen item from him, he is also executed for it. Granted, with regard to the first clause it can be explained that although there is no obligation to return the item, the gentile is executed because he caused the Jew distress; but with regard to the latter clause, what did the second gentile do? He did not cause the Jew distress, and since the item is worth less than one peruta, one is not obligated to return it unless he stole it from a gentile. Consequently, the second theft should not be considered a legally significant act.

Avodah Zarah 72a:3.english: Rather, should one not conclude from it that pulling an item acquires it in a transaction performed by a gentile? Accordingly, the actions of both the first and second gentiles are legally significant acts of theft, for which they are liable to be executed. The Gemara affirms: Conclude from it that this is so.

Jastrow, מְנָת 1.english:
מְנָת f. (Biblical Hebrew; מָנָה)
1) portion, share. Bava Batra 12ᵃ מ׳ בכרם וכ׳ I sell thee a portion of my vineyard.—מְנַת המלך the king’s share (annona). Nedarim 62ᵇ; Bava Batra 8ᵃ, see מִנְדָּה. Pirkei Avot Zar. 71ᵃ הפס עלי מ׳ מלך settle for me the annona (in kind or money).

—2) appointment; בִּמְנַת, עַל מְנַת (abbrev. ע"מ) on condition that, for the sake of. Tosefta Demai VI, 13 ואם התנה עמו במ׳ כן ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant … מתחלה ע"מ לעשות כן) but if he originally had made that agreement (of dividing the profits) with him. Ib. VII, 3 ע"מ שהמעשרות שלי with the condition that the tithes be mine. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia V, 10ᵇ bottom of page במ׳ לעלות לו וכ׳ with the condition that he will give him (as his share) one newborn animal or one crop of wool. Pirkei Avot I, 3, see עֶבֶד. Tosefta Sanhedrin XI, 2 יודע אני וע"מ כן אני עושה I know (the nature of the offense and its penalty), and on that condition I am committing it; Mekhilta Mishpatim section (Parashah) 20 יודע אני ע"מ כן (read: וע"מ). Kiddushin 6ᵇ מתנה ע"מ להחזיר a present made with the condition that it shall be returned (possession for the time being); and see from—Avodah Zarah 37ᵃ, and from כל האומר ע"מ … מעכשיו דמי if a man says ‘on condition’, it is to be considered as if he had said ‘from now’, i.e. the stipulated transaction takes retrospective effect when the condition is fulfilled.—Bava Batra X, 8 (175ᵇ) על מְנָתוֹ הלוהו Arukh (ed. אמונתו, see אֱמוּנָה) he extended the loan to him (the friend) on the condition which he (the guarantor) offered.

Jastrow, פִּיס 1.english:
פִּיס (compare פָּסַס) to split, divide, distribute.

Hifil - הֵפִיס
1) to penetrate, (compare בָּדַק); to cause abdominal trouble. Pesachim 107ᵃ מִיסְרָן ומֵפִיס this drink is a tempter and then gives pain (Manuscript Munich ומֵיפֵיס; Manuscript Oxford מייסרן ומיפיס, see פָּסַס; ed. ומפייס, see infra).—[מפיס מורסא, see פָּסַס.]

—2) to break a person’s anger or will, to pacify, persuade, comfort. Shevuot 45ᵃ כדי להָפִיס דעתו וכ׳ in order to satisfy the mind of the employer (to convince him that he was mistaken). Yerushalmi ib. VIII, 38ᵈ top; Yerushalmi Sanhedrin III, 21ᶜ bottom of page מצוה להֲפִיסוֹ it is proper to give him (the owner of the lost animal) satisfaction (by stating the cause of the loss); see Piël—Avodah Zarah 71ᵃ צא והָפֵס עלי מנת המלך go and satisfy for me the royal taxes (settle for me as best you can), see מְנָת.

—3) to arbitrate, decide (compare פָּסַק). Shabbat 33ᵃ מי מֵפִיס who will decide (as to the cause of my disease)? Ib. 54ᵃ מי מפיס וכ׳ who will decide which udders are tied up for the purpose of drying them up and which for the purpose of preserving the milk?—Especially to decide by chance, by drawing lots, counting a certain number &c. (see פַּיִיס). Tamid I, 2 מי שטבל יבוא ויָפִיס let those who have bathed, come and take part in the count of chance; הֵפִיסוּ זכה וכ׳ after they have drawn, he who has won, has won (no appeal is permitted). Yoma 24ᵇ למה מְפִיסִין וחוזרין וכ׳ why did they draw once and again (why not at once for all the functions to be distributed)? Ib. במה מפיסין (Rashi: מפייסין) what garments do they wear when drawing? Bereishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 84 (play on פסים, Bereishit XXXVII, 23) שהפיסו עליה וכ׳ they drew lots about it (the coat) as to who should carry it to his father &c. Shabbat XXIII, 2 (148ᵇ) מפיס (אדם) עם וכ׳ a man may decide by lot (on the Sabbath) the shares of honor at the table &c.; ib. 149ᵇ; and elsewhere.

Piël - פִּיֵּיס to pacify, conciliate, persuade. Pesachim l. common gender. מְיַסְּרָן ומְפַיֵּיס (that drink) chastises us (gives us pain), and yet is so persuasive (tempting). Berakhot 28ᵇ אני יכול לפַיְּיסוֹ בדברים וכ׳ I might appease him with words or bribe him with money. Bava Batra 9ᵇ כל הנותן … והמְפַיְּיסוֹ בדברים וכ׳ he who gives a poor man a coin will be blessed with six blessings, but he who speaks kindly to him, will be blessed with eleven blessings. Bereishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 93, end כשם שלא פ׳ … אלא וכ׳ as Joseph pacified his brothers only by weeping &c. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin l. common gender. מצוה להפיסו … ואינו מְפַיְּיסוֹ על שקר it is right to satisfy his mind by stating the truth, but one must not do so by a falsehood; Yerushalmi Shevuot l. common gender. מפייסו … אינו מפייסו וכ׳. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 19, end נלך ונְפַיֵּיס לגדלת, see גַּדֶּלֶת; and from—Bereishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 94, end ופייליה, read: ופִיְּיסוּהוּ and they appeased him (Nebuchadnezzar).—Part. pass. מְפוּיָּיס. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 51 הריני מפ׳ שמחלת וכ׳ I am convinced that thou hast forgiven Israel.

Hithpaël - הִתְפַּיֵּיס,

Nithpaël - נִתְפַּיֵּיס to be appeased, satisfied, persuaded. Ib. אותה שעה נֵתְפַּיְּיסוּ … על וכ׳ now all Israelites were satisfied with regard to the work of the Tabernacle (that everything was correct). Berakhot 33ᵃ נתפ׳ אותו השר that prince’s anger was appeased. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 10 הרי הגורן בא והכל מִתְפַּיְּיסִים בשביל וכ׳ when harvesting time comes, all (that now are disputing) will be convinced for whose sake the field has been sown. Yoma 86ᵇ ספק מִתְפַּיֵּיס הימנו וכ׳ it is doubtful whether he will or will not accept his apology; ספק מתפייס בדברים וכ׳ it is doubtful whether he will be appeased by mere words (without demanding a fine or public satisfaction) &c.; and from

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:1.english: Karkom - We translate it as a siege, karkomin.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:2.hebrew: כל כהנות - הנמצאות בתוכה פסולות לבעליהן, דאשת כהן אסורה אף באונס, אבל אשת ישראל לא. הא הכא דשעת מלחמה היא וקתני אסורות, דיש פנאי לבעול:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:2.english: All the women married to priests - Those found within it are disqualified from their husbands, for a priest's wife is forbidden even if raped, but an Israelite's wife is not. Here, it is wartime, and it teaches that they are forbidden, because there is leisure to engage in intercourse.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:3.english: They do not have time to pour libations - Because the inclination for libation is not strong for them, and they are preoccupied with war.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:4.english: They have time to engage in intercourse - Because their inclination is strong for them.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:2:1.hebrew: מותר לומר לו תן לנו את דמיה - דהא לא קנו לה, והוא אינו חייב להן אלא מעות. ותניא לעיל (עבודה זרה דף סד.): ישראל שנושה בעובד כוכבים מנה, מכר עבודת כוכבים והביא לו יין נסך, והביא לו — מותר:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:2:1.english: It is permitted for them to say to him: Give us its monetary value - for the Jewish craftsmen did not acquire the barrel, and the gentile owes them only money. And it was taught above (Avodah Zarah 64a): If an Israelite was owed a *maneh* by a gentile, and the gentile sold an idol and brought the Israelite wine used for a libation, it is permitted for the Israelite to accept it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:3:1.hebrew: צא והפס עלי מנת המלך - ארנונא שהיו נותנין מתבואותיהן ומבהמותיהן עישור; וישראל זה שחייב לתת למלך יין, מותר לומר לעובד כוכבים: הפס עלי, אף על גב דקא יהיב האי עובד כוכבים יין נסך והאי ישראל הוא פרעיה דמיה, כיון דהוה מצי לסלוקי לשליחא דמלכא בזוזי, כי יהיב ליה עובד כוכבים יין נסך לאו שלוחיה דישראל הוא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:4:1.hebrew: עול תחתי לעוצר - היכנס במקומי להפיס את השוטר, כמו ״זה יעצור בעמי״ (שמואל א ט׳:י״ז). לשון אחר: לשון אוצר, שממונה על אוצרות יין ושמן של מלך לגבות ולאצור:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:4:2.hebrew: עול תחתי קאמרת - כיון דאמר ליה ״עול תחתי״, הוי משמע: הוי במקומי, וכל מאי דיהיב ליה עובד כוכבים הוי כאילו יהביה ישראל, דהא במקומו הוא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:4:3.english: This - Rav Yehuda's statement is only comparable to the latter part of the baraita.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:4:4.hebrew: אבל אומר לו מלטני מן העוצר - דאפשר לסלוקיה בזוזי, הלכך למיתב ליה חמרא לאו שלוחיה הוא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:5:1.hebrew: המוכר יינו לעובד כוכבים פסק - עמו מעות עד שלא מדד, דמיו מותרין. מפרש בגמרא טעמא: איכא דמוקי לה משום משיכה, בעובד כוכבים קנה. הלכך כשמודד, היינו משיכה וקנייה עובד כוכבים מיד, דהוה ליה לישראל זוזי גבי דעובד כוכבים בהלואה, ויין נסך לא הוי עד דנגע ביה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:5:1.english: One who sells his wine to an idol worshipper, if he fixed [the price] - with him, money, before he measured, its money is permitted. The Gemara explains the reason: there are those who establish it based on *meshikha* (pulling/drawing), that an idol worshipper acquires through it. Therefore, when he measures, that is the *meshikha* and the idol worshipper's acquisition immediately, and the Jew has the money from the idol worshipper as a loan, and it does not become libation wine until he touches it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:5:2.hebrew: מדד עד שלא פסק דמיו אסורין - דעובד כוכבים לא קנייה במשיכה, דכיון דלא פסק דמיו לא סמכה דעתיה. הלכך כי נגע ביה, הוי יין נסך דישראל. ואיכא דמוקי לה כשהקדים לו עובד כוכבים מעות לישראל, ובגמרא מפרש לה:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:5:2.english: He measured before he fixed [the price], its money is forbidden - because the idol worshipper did not acquire it through *meshikha*, for since he did not fix the price, his mind was not settled. Therefore, when he touched it, it became libation wine belonging to the Jew. And there are those who establish it as a case where the idol worshipper gave money to the Jew in advance, and the Gemara explains this.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:6:1.hebrew: משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה - אע"ג דלא יהיב עובד כוכבים דמי לישראל משיך מיניה קנייה וכן ישראל מעובד' כוכבים:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:6:3.hebrew: ולא הדרי בהו - השולחין אלמא במשיכה קנינהו המקבלין. לאידך גיסא מתשובת הגאונים פרדשני מי שיש לו כור חיטין למכור פוסק דמים ללוקח והולך לביתו ומשגר לו קב חיטין לראות כמה הן יפות ואם מעכב הלוקח אותו קב אצלו מתקיים המקח ואם אינו חפץ בהן מחזירו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71a:6:4.hebrew: רב אשי אמר אינה קונה - אלא במתן מעות קנו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:10:1.hebrew: סיפא לאו מקח טעות - בתמיה. ואף על גב דיהיב דמי לישקלינהו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:10:2.hebrew: מיחזי כעבודת כוכבים - לכי הדר שקל זוזי מיחזי כמאן דמזבן לעבודת כוכבים דמי:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:11:1.hebrew: פסק עד שלא מדד דמיו מותרין - דכי מדד קניה עובד כוכבים במשיכה וקמו זוזי בהלואה גביה יין נסך לא הוי עד דנגע ביה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:11:2.hebrew: שהקדים לו דינר - שנתן לו מעותיו קודם לכן:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:12:1.hebrew: שהקדים לו - ונתן לו מעות יותר מכדי דמי היין עד שיפסוק הדמים יחזיר לו ישראל את המותר: אמאי דמיו אסורין:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:13:1.hebrew: ולדידך דאמרת - טעמא דרישא משום דמשיכה קונה סיפא נמי אמאי דמיו אסורין:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:14:2.hebrew: לא פסק - קודם משיכה לא סמכא דעתיה למקנייה במשיכה שמא ירבה לו בדמיו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:1.hebrew: בן נח - שגזל את ישראל פחות משוה פרוטה אף על גב דגבי ישראל לאו ממונא הוא דמחלי עליה גבי עובד כוכבים ממונא הוא ובן נח נצטוה על הגזל בסנהדרין (דף נו.) ואזהרה שלהן זו היא מיתתן ואין צריכין התראה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:2.hebrew: ולא ניתן להישבון - ולא מחייב לאהדורה להאי ישראל דהא מחיל עליה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:3.hebrew: אמאי נהרג - הא לא קניא להך גזילה וכל היכא דאיתא של ישראל היא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:1:1.hebrew: מדמשכיה עובד כוכבים - במדה קנייה ואף על גב דלא יהב זוזי והוו להו זוזי הלואה גביה מקמי דניהוי יין נסך דהא לא הוי נסך עד שנגע ביה ואפילו אי לא שקלי זוזי מינייהו שפיר דמי:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:2:1.hebrew: במנא דעובד כוכבים - דיין שבכלי אוסרו והוי יין נסך מקמי משיכה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:3:1.hebrew: מדמטי לאוירא דמנא - דעובד כוכבים קנייה עובד כוכבים בהגבהה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:5:1.hebrew: שמעת מיניה וכולי - ואנן איבעיא לן בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פה:):

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:6:1.hebrew: עכבת יין - אוגנים יש בכליו של עובד כוכבים שמתעכב היין על פיו כטיפה או כשני טיפין מקמי דנימטי חמרא דישראל באוירא דמנא דעובד כוכבים ומיתסר בההיא טיפת יין שעל פיו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:6:2.hebrew: דכוזנתא - פך קטנה מחבית כדאמר במועד קטן (דף יב.) זופתין כוזנתא ואין זופתין חביתא במועד:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:7:1.hebrew: כמאן - הא דאמר רב למישקל דמי ברישא מקמי דניתסר בההיא עכבה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:7:2.hebrew: דלא כרבן שמעון בן גמליאל - דקתני במתניתין יין נסך שנפל לבור כולו אסור רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר ימכר כולו לעובדי כוכבים חוץ מדמי יין נסך שבו אלמא משום תערובת יין נסך לא מיתסר בהנאה חמרא דישראל ואנן קיימא לן כל מקום ששנה רבן שמעון במשנתנו הלכה כמותו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:8:1.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא אלא לרב - הך קושיא למאן רמיית ליה אלא לרב דאמר לסבוייתא למישקל דמי ברישא לדידיה לא תירמיה דאיהו אמר בהדיא דאין הלכה כרבן שמעון:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:8:2.english: Rather, in the case of a barrel that was mixed with other barrels, one takes one of them and throws it into the river, and the others are permitted for benefit.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:8:3.hebrew: אבל לא יין ביין - דכי נתערב יין נסך ביין כשר כולו אסור. ואי קשיא אביי ורבא היכי מיתרצי אתקפתיה דאמימר הא אינהו הוו קשישי מיניה טובא לא תיקשי דהא במסכת בכורות (דף יג:) תרצינהו אביי ורבא להנך שינויי אליבא דרבי יוחנן דאליביה קאמר אמימר לשמעתיה וקבעוה בעלי תלמוד כאן אמילתיה דאמימר:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:9:2.hebrew: יחזיר - דלא קנייה ולא מיחייב לבערה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:9:3.hebrew: יוליך לים המלח - דכיון דלא מצי לאהדוריה ולמשקל דמי:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:9:4.hebrew: מקח טעות - הויא משיכה בטעות דלאו אדעתא דעבודת כוכבים זבן:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 72a:1:1.hebrew: ומאי לא ניתן להישבון - הא לא שייך ביה הישבון דכיון דעובד כוכבים לא קנייה דישראל היא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 72a:1:2.hebrew: אינה בתורת הישבון - כלומר הכי נמי קאמר אינה בתורת שום גזילה דעובד כוכבים דכל היכא דאיתא דמרה היא. והוא הדין לשוה פרוטה והאי דנקט פחות לאשמועינן דנהרג עליה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 72a:3:1.hebrew: אלא שמע מינה משיכה קונה - הלכך קניה קמא והדר קניה האי ונהרג על שגזל. ולא ניתן להישבון דרישא דוקא פחות משוה פרוטה דישראל מחיל ולא מיחייב עובד כוכבים לאהדורה:

Shulchan Arukh, Choshen Mishpat 200:3.hebrew: כליו של אדם כל מקום שיש לו רשות להניחו קנה לו וכיון שנכנסו המטלטלים בתוך הכלי אין אחד מהם יכול לחזור בו והרי זה כמי שהונחו בתוך ביתו: (הגה ויש מחלקין דאם אינם ברשות לוקח רק בסימטא וכיוצא בזה אין כליו קונים אלא אם כן מדד או עד שיאמר לו זיל וקני (טור ותוס' והרא"ש פרק הספינה והגהות מיימוני פ"ד דמכירה) )לפיכך אין כליו של אדם קונים לו ברשות הרבים ולא ברשות המוכר אלא אלא אם כן אמר לו המקנה לך וקנה בכלי זה ואז קנה אם הוא ברשות המוכר:
Shulchan Arukh, Choshen Mishpat 200:3.english: A person's vessels, wherever he has permission to place them, acquire for him. And once the movable property has entered the vessel, neither of them can retract, and it is as if they were placed inside his house. (Gloss: And there are those who distinguish that if they are not in the buyer's domain but only in a public alleyway and the like, his vessels do not acquire unless he measured or until he says to him, 'Go and acquire' (Tur and Tosafot and Rosh, chapter 'HaSfinah' and Hagahot Maimoni, chapter 4 of 'Mechira')). Therefore, a person's vessels do not acquire for him in a public domain, nor in the seller's domain, unless the seller says to him, 'Go and acquire with this vessel,' and then he acquires if it is in the seller's domain.

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 132:2.english: When an Israelite has sold his wine to a gentile, he may benefit from the money received if the wine has not yet been delivered, because the wine is prohibited only from the moment the gentile has touched it, which he could not have done before delivery. But if the gentile took the wine before the final conclusion of the transaction, it is forbidden for the Israelite to benefit from the money received; the gentile having touched the wine before payment, this sale is assimilated to that of the wine intended for idols. <small>GLOSS</small>: As soon as the wine belongs to the gentile, the Israelite no longer has any right to supervise the liquid, and there is reason to fear that the idolater may have touched it. This is only a question of the case where the Israelite measured the wine into his own vessel or into that of the gentile which has no impediment. But if the Israelite measured the liquid into the gentile's vessel equipped with a device that can slow down the transfer of wine, or into his own vessel held and agitated by the gentile to facilitate the flow of wine, if the Israelite wishes in this case to benefit from the price of his merchandise, he must receive the money before measuring the wine, whether the gentile shakes the vessel left on the ground, or takes it in his hands. However, if the Israelite measured the wine into the vessel belonging to the gentile, and carrying a device that allowed a small part of the liquid first poured by the gentile to remain in the vessel, a mixture was formed in which the gentile's liquid renders forbidden the wine subsequently poured by the Israelite; however, in a case of *fait accompli*, it is permitted to benefit from all the wine poured into the vessel, minus a quantity equal to that of the liquid belonging to the gentile that remained in the container. But, deliberately, the gentile's wine renders forbidden that of the Israelite when the liquid belonging to the gentile is in the vessel itself, but if it is on the rim, whether the vessel is in the gentile's courtyard or in the hands of its owner, or if the Israelite, the wine being in his courtyard, asks the gentile to sell him his vessel, then the wine that the Israelite pours into the vessel is permitted, because it belongs to him as soon as it has touched the liquid on the rim of the container. Likewise, if the gentile, while the Israelite is measuring wine for him, lifted the vessel to show that it belongs to him, the wine is permitted, because the gentile touched it before it was measured: but if the gentile did not lift the vessel containing the wine that the Israelite was to measure, the same law applies to this liquid as to any other wine coming from a gentile. These laws were in force at the time when gentiles offered wine to idols; but as nowadays, there are no more gentiles, it is always permitted to benefit from wine touched by a gentile who does not practice his religion. Such is the usage generally adopted and these laws are no longer applied.

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 132:3.english: Jewish laborers who performed work for a gentile, and the gentile sent them a barrel of wine as their wage: if they had not yet accepted it as their wage, it is permitted for them to say to him: 'Instead of sending us this barrel, let it be yours, and you give us its monetary value' (Ran). But if they accepted it as their wage, it is forbidden (R' Yerucham and Rosh). (And see below, section 123, that even after accepting it, it is permitted nowadays).

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 132:5.english: When an Israelite wine merchant must give a portion of his wine to his lord, he is permitted to ask a gentile to be his intermediary with the lord to obtain the favor of being discharged from his tribute, if, to appease the lord, the gentile offers him wine intended for idols. The Israelite may later compensate the gentile; but it is forbidden for the Israelite to instruct a gentile to give, in his name, wine intended for idols.

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 132:6.english: If a lord was distributing his wine to the people with the intention of obtaining money from them, it is forbidden for an Israelite to give a certain sum to a gentile for the latter to go to the lord's treasury to receive wine on behalf of the Israelite. However, it is permitted for the Israelite to have the gentile carry a sum of money, as a contribution, to escape the lord's demands.

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 146:3.english: When an Israelite has bought scrap metal from a gentile, he may refuse it if he finds an idol in it after having paid for the merchandise before delivery; the same applies if he received it without paying for it immediately, because there is an error, the Israelite not having believed he would find an idol in his purchase. But if the scrap metal has been delivered and paid for, the Israelite no longer has the right to refuse it and is obliged to throw it into the sea.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Avodah Zarah 71.english: And not only because the barrel did not reach the Jewish craftsmen's hands and they did not acquire it, but also the money the Jewish craftsmen receive from the gentile is not in exchange for the barrel, because the gentile owes them only money for their wage. And the Ra'avad wrote that if the gentile stipulated with the Jewish craftsmen to give them wine as their wage, then he owes them wine.

Rashi explains that this is referring to a situation where the gentile could also settle the debt with money, and he is not considered the Jew’s emissary if he pays with wine used for a libation instead. Tosafot also note that if the gentile can settle the debt with money or in some other manner, it is certainly permitted. Rabbeinu Tam, in Sefer HaYashar, likewise rules that if the government does not demand that it be paid specifically in wine, there is certainly no problem. He explains that even if the Jew must settle the debt by paying with wine, since the Jew does not instruct the gentile to pay with wine but to settle the debt in any way he can, this is sufficient to disconnect the Jew from the wine itself.

For when he returns the idol worship to the gentile without receiving money, it does not appear as a commercial transaction. But when he returns idol worship to the gentile and receives money from him, it appears (even though it is not truly so) as if he is selling idol worship to the gentile (Rashi).

That the gentile's touching of the wine occurred after the wine had already passed into the gentile's possession and he became obligated for its payment. And merely fixing the price certainly does not transfer ownership of the wine to the gentile, but rather with an act of acquisition ('pulling'). If so, pulling is what acquires (and it cannot be said that he gave him the money before measuring, and with that the wine was acquired, for if so, the money would certainly be permitted, since the gentile did not touch the wine beforehand).

And as mentioned above, some explained that the act of acquisition occurred when the gentile lifted the wine in the measuring vessel before measuring it into his own vessels, and by the measuring itself, he rendered the wine forbidden (Rabbeinu Chananel, Ra'avad). And some explained that by the measuring itself, the wine was acquired by the gentile, and the wine was rendered forbidden by his touching it afterwards (Rashi and others).

And then the acquisition is completed by pulling, or by giving money. But when the price is not fixed, even if he gives an advance payment, it is not a complete sale, for it is possible that they will not agree on the price and will cancel the entire sale.

One of the seven Noahide commandments is the prohibition of theft, and a descendant of Noah who transgresses one of his commandments is liable to death. And even though for a Jew, only from the value of a *peruta* and above is it considered theft (which carries an obligation of restitution), the Gemara in Tractate Sanhedrin (57a) states that for less than a *peruta*, a person waives his money, but descendants of Noah do not waive it at all, even for less than a *peruta* (see Rashi there). And the Rambam wrote that for a Jew there are fixed measures in various laws (many of which are *Halakha* to Moses from Sinai), and for less than the measure there is no obligation. Therefore, since less than a *peruta* is not considered money at all for a Jew, the laws of theft and robbery and the like do not apply to it. But these measures were not given to gentiles, and therefore they are liable even for less than a *peruta*.

And in Tractate Sanhedrin (57a), the matter was defined as a permissible clarification, that even though he is not obligated to return the stolen item because the Jew waived it, nevertheless, at the time of the theft itself, he caused him distress (see Rashi there). And in Tosafot Eruvin (62a), they explain that this is not because of the Jew's distress itself, for a descendant of Noah is not liable to death for that reason, but rather because for the gentile himself, even less than a *peruta* is considered significant property, meaning he himself committed a transgression.

That is to say, if the Jewish wine seller measured the wine into his own vessel, and then the gentile pulled it and acquired the wine — indeed, the wine was not rendered forbidden before the gentile acquired it. And the commentators noted that the law would be the same even in the gentile's own vessel, as long as it does not contain his wine.

And they asked: How is acquisition performed by the gentile holding the object in his hand? For even though Rashi says that the gentile acquires by lifting (which is one of the methods of acquisition), here the act of lifting was not performed on the acquired object (in our case, the wine) but on the vessel, which is already the gentile's! And the Ritv'a explains that since we assume that something that will eventually rest in a vessel is considered as if it is already resting in it, then the aiming and stabilizing of the vessel so that the wine does not spill from it are considered part of the act of lifting, not only for the vessel but also for the wine being poured into it.

For Rav distinguishes between a mixture where the forbidden item exists by itself, but we do not know how to identify where it is (e.g., one barrel of *yayin nesekh* was mixed with several barrels of kosher wine), and a mixture where the forbidden and permitted items are actually mixed together, like liquid in liquid, wine in wine. And Rav holds that a mixture where the forbidden item is present throughout is more stringent than a doubt whether the forbidden item has come into one's possession.

The early commentators, both from examining our *sugya* and from comparing it with the parallel *sugya* in Tractate Bechorot, conclude that the opinion of the questioner is that regarding a gentile, acquisition is only by performing both methods together, both giving money and pulling (Tosafot, Ramban, and other early commentators).

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Avodah Zarah 72.english: Rashi explains that according to this opinion, this law should not be understood as referring to theft of less than a *peruta*, as the questioner thought. Rather, there is a general statement here concerning any theft by a descendant of Noah, including one that is worth a *peruta*, to say that since he does not acquire by pulling, it is not subject to the law of theft and restitution. Other commentators (Ra'avad) explain that the intention is that since he is executed only because he caused distress to the Jew, and not because he actually acquired the stolen item, there is no remedy for this by returning the stolen item, although he is certainly obligated to return it to its owner. And the Ritv'a noted that this explanation also fits the conclusion of the *sugya*, that a gentile acquires by pulling.

For he does not cause distress to the Jew, for he did not steal from him. And he is also not considered as taking property that is not his, because the Jew has already waived it after it was stolen by the first one (since it is less than a *peruta*), and there is no place to call him a thief (Ra'avad), unless the first gentile acquired the stolen item by pulling, and therefore it is considered as if he stole it from him.

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Avodah Zarah 71.english: The Tosafot asked: Perhaps it can be said that here the matter refers to after the war, when they have leisure! And they answered that the language of the Mishna is general, and implies whether the matter was during the war or after it. However, Rabbeinu Tam writes (in Sefer HaYashar) that the meaning of the Mishna there is specifically during wartime, to say that all the priestesses who were in the city at the time it was conquered are forbidden, even if they left there afterwards, as is also proven from the continuation of the Mishna there.

Tosafot wrote that this is not the source for Ameimar's statement, from what the Persians practice. Rather, this is his general reasoning, and he brings it as a kind of hint to the matter, for the Persians act this way, and presumably, it is an ancient custom that has a basis in the Torah (see Rashba).

Rashi explains (on the next page) that according to the opinion of the questioner (and also the conclusion of the discussion), this *halakha* refers specifically to less than a *peruta*, and 'it is not subject to restitution' in the sense that he is not obligated to return it to the Jew, because since it is less than a *peruta*, the Jew waives it and there is no obligation of restitution. But if a gentile stole from a gentile, since he does not waive it at all, he is certainly obligated to return it. And in another place (Eruvin 62a), Rashi explains the matter not specifically in relation to less than a *peruta*; there he explains that the reason it is not subject to restitution is because of '*kim lei b'drabba minei*' (he is subject to the more severe penalty), that since he is liable to death, he no longer has a monetary obligation. And see Tosafot, who rejected this explanation. And in the Aruch (entry 'Ben Noah'), he explained that the intention is that returning the stolen item to its owner does not help him to be exempt from death. And see on the next page.

The ruling permitting the money paid for the wine if the Jewish seller agrees with the gentile buyer on the price before measuring the wine applies in the case where the Jew measures the wine into his own vessel, or, according to the *Tur*, into the gentile’s vessel if there were no remnants of wine left in it. But if the Jew measures the wine into the gentile’s vessel containing wine, or into a Jew’s vessel in the hand of the gentile, he must receive the money before he measures the wine into the vessel, because the gentile can acquire the wine either by pulling or by giving payment. If the Jew measures the wine into the vessel before taking the payment, the money is forbidden, because when the wine reaches the vessel it is rendered forbidden as nondescript wine of gentiles. This is in accordance with the ruling of the Rambam, who holds that a stream of liquid serves as a connection (*Kesef Mishne*, *Leĥem Mishne*). The *Shulĥan Arukh* does not deem the money forbidden and regards a stream of liquid as a connection only with regard to rendering it prohibited to drink the wine (Rambam *Sefer Kedusha*, *Hilkhot Ma’akhalot Assurot* 13:24; *Shulĥan Arukh*, *Yoreh De’a* 132:2, and see 124:17–18).

A Jew who sells wine and measures his wine into a gentile's vessel, if the gentile held the vessel in his hand, or if it was in the seller's domain and the seller said to him: 'Let your vessels acquire for you,' or if the vessel was in the gentile's courtyard, even if there was wine at the bottom of the gentile's vessel — it is permitted *ab initio* to measure and then take the payment for the wine, for as soon as the wine enters the airspace of the vessel, the gentile acquired it, and it was not rendered forbidden until it reached the wine at the bottom of the vessel. And similarly, if the gentile himself measured the wine and first lifted it to acquire it, everything is permitted, for he acquired it first before measuring. (Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 124:17-18 in the gloss).

It is certainly a mistaken transaction, for if he had known that idol worship was there, he would not have bought it. However, in addition to that, there is no concern here for *marit ayin* (appearance of impropriety), since he has not yet paid. And see Rashi, who apparently did not read 'demiḥazi ki'.

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Avodah Zarah 72.english: See in the versions that many early commentators read here: 'If so, why is it not subject to restitution?' And the Ra'avad explained that if pulling acquires for a gentile, it is necessary to say that he is not obligated to return it to the Jew — either because the Jew waives it, or because it is not subject to the obligation of 'and he shall return the stolen item.' But if he did not acquire it at all, what need is there to say this? For it belongs to the Jew wherever it is!

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Avodah Zarah 71.english: In Tractate Ketubot, there is another answer that was not brought here, which distinguishes between a karkom of the same kingdom and a karkom of another kingdom (and the matter was explained in opposite ways: some explained that a karkom of another kingdom fears that the enemy will come at any moment, and therefore has no leisure, which is not the case for a karkom of the same kingdom. Others explained the opposite, that the king of the same kingdom does not allow soldiers to break order, which is not the case for a karkom of another kingdom). Rabbeinu Tam wrote that it is the way of the Gemara, when bringing a topic from another place, to take only one answer that seems to them a better answer (Sefer HaYashar). However, the Ritv'a wrote that that answer did not relate at all to our Mishna, in which there is no difference what kind of karkom it was. And so, the Tosafot wrote there, but they explained that in our case, it is specifically a karkom of another kingdom.

There are several interpretations for this matter. In the first interpretation, Rashi explains that here it refers to the giving of gifts, which they give to each other and do not retract. However, as Tosafot noted, there is a difficulty with this interpretation, because there is no proof from here for buying and selling, which involves an obligation of payment. In another interpretation (in the name of the Geonim), Rashi explains that it was their custom that when a person buys a large quantity of a certain commodity, the seller sends him a small quantity as a sample, and if the buyer agrees to this, the sale is concluded. Rabbeinu Tam explains that it refers to gifts that a person sends to his friend so that the latter will also pay him with gifts. Even if his friend does not reciprocate generously as he sent him, he does not retract. And the Ritv'a brings similarly in the name of Tosafot that these are gifts that were sent to ministers and rulers so that they would take care of their affairs, and even if the handling of their affairs is delayed, they do not retract.

For if pulling does not acquire, then even though the property is actually in the gentile's hands, it is not considered his, and it will not be considered theft for him. And simply, the question is why he is executed at all for theft, and not specifically for less than a *peruta* (and see in Tosefot Chullin). Indeed, Tosafot asked: Even a Jew who steals from a Jew does not acquire the stolen item to be his, and even so, he is liable regarding the laws of damages, that it is considered as if it belongs to the thief and he pays everything. If so, regarding a gentile, he would be liable to death even though the money did not pass into his possession! Therefore, they explained that if the stolen item was worth a *peruta*, it would be understandable. But since it was a theft of less than a *peruta*, where the victim did not lose anything, and the thief also did not acquire it — it is as if nothing was done. And the Ritv'a inferred from Rashi's words that the main difficulty is from the fact that this theft was not subject to restitution, meaning he is not obligated to return it. From this, it must be proven that he acquired it, for if not, why is he not obligated to return it? For it belongs to the Jew wherever it is. And it turns out that even according to this approach, the main difficulty is from theft of less than a *peruta*.

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Avodah Zarah 71.english: According to Rav Ashi, the fact that they do not retract these gifts is not because they believe an act of acquisition was performed by pulling. Rather, it is a custom of haughtiness (or in other words, a custom related to their perception of honor, that they do not return a gift), and therefore nothing can be proven from here regarding methods of acquisition.

Steinsaltz comment #6 on Avodah Zarah 71.english: A descendant of Noah who stole (whether from a gentile or from a Jew) is liable to death. And a descendant of Noah is liable even for theft of less than a *peruta*. And similarly, if another gentile came and stole from the first thief — both are liable. (Rambam, Sefer Shoftim, Hilkhot Melakhim, chapter 9, *halakha* 9).

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:1.english: GEMARA: We learned in our Mishna that during wartime, soldiers do not have leisure, and there is no concern that they committed a transgression. And the Gemara raises a contradiction to this from what we learned in another Mishna: A city that was conquered by a karkom (an army laying siege to a city) — all the wives of priests within it are disqualified, as we are concerned that they may have been raped by the soldiers, even though it is wartime! Rav Mari said: They do not have leisure to pour libations, because they are concerned about the war, and the inclination for libation is not strong at that time. But they have leisure to engage in intercourse, because this inclination is strong, even during wartime.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:2.english: MISHNA: Jewish craftsmen (meaning, Israelites) to whom a gentile sent a barrel of wine used for a libation as their wage (in exchange for their work), and it is forbidden for benefit — it is permitted for them to say to him: “Give us its monetary value,” how much the barrel is worth. But if the barrel has entered their possession — it is forbidden to receive its value from the gentile, for this is as if they sold libation wine and benefited from its value.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:3.english: ג גמרא Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: It is permitted for a person to say to a gentile: Go and placate the governmental tax for me. That is to say, endeavor for me to appease the authorities who collect the tax on wine, and I will reimburse you afterwards. This is permitted even if that gentile pays the tax with wine used for a libation.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:4.english: They raised an objection to this from what we learned in a baraita: A person may not say to a gentile: Go in my stead to the *otzer* (commissary)! That is to say, pay in my place to the wine collector, when the gentile pays with wine used for a libation! Rav said to him: Are you saying "Go in my stead to the *otzer*"? Since the Jew says in the language "in my stead," it is as if the gentile is doing it in his place. This case is not similar except to that which we learned, but a person may say to a gentile: "Save me from the *otzer*." That is to say, find a way to save me from this tax by you paying the tax collector. For Rav is not speaking of a case where the Jew asks the gentile to enter in his place, but only that the gentile save him.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:5.english: One who sells his wine to a non-Jew: if he fixed (determined and agreed upon) the price before he measured the amount of wine sold into the non-Jew's vessels — the money for the wine is permitted, and he is not considered as one who sells libation wine, for the non-Jew purchased the wine before it became forbidden, and the money already belonged to the Jew. But if he measured the wine into the non-Jew's vessels, and it already became forbidden, before he fixed the price, before the wine was acquired by the non-Jew — its money is forbidden, because he became like one who sells libation wine, from which benefit is prohibited.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:6.english: GEMARA: Ameimar says: Acquiring by pulling applies to a gentile, meaning that when a gentile pulls an object for the purpose of acquisition, the acquisition is completed by the act of pulling itself. Know that it is so, as those Persians send pardashnei to one another and do not retract them, which implies that they acquire from one another by pulling alone! Rav Ashi says: Actually, I will say to you that pulling an object does not acquire it in a transaction involving a gentile, and the fact that they do not retract their gifts is not due to the laws of acquisition, but because haughtiness has taken hold of them, and they consider it shameful to retract a gift.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71a:7.english: Rav Ashi said: From where do I say that pulling does not acquire for a gentile? It is from that which Rav said to those wine shopkeepers: When you measure wine for gentiles, take the zuzim from them and then measure the wine for them. And if they do not have zuzim with them readily available, lend them zuzim and then take those zuzim back from them, so that it will be a loan provided to them that they are repaying. As if you do not do so, when it becomes wine used for a libation, it becomes so in your possession, and when you take payment for it, you are taking payment for wine used for a libation. And if it enters your mind that acquiring by pulling applies to a gentile,

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:1.english: From the moment the gentile pulled it, he acquired it, whereas it did not become wine used for a libation until he touched it. Therefore, the seller can receive the price of the wine he sold, for at the time of the acquisition, the wine was permitted!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:10.english: Rava said: And why in the second case, where he gave zuzim, can he not return it? Is the first clause a mistaken transaction, but the latter clause not a mistaken transaction? Rather, Rava said: The first clause and the latter clause are both mistaken transactions. Therefore, in the first clause, where he did not yet give zuzim, it does not appear as idol worship in the hand of a Jew, and therefore he can return it. Whereas in the latter clause, where he did give zuzim, it appears as idol worship in the hand of a Jew, and due to the appearance of impropriety, he is obligated to destroy it.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:11.english: And now they bring proofs against Rav Ashi's opinion, who holds that a gentile does not acquire by pulling. Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear a proof from our Mishna, where we learned: One who sells his wine to a gentile, if he fixed its price before he measured — its money is permitted, since the wine was already acquired by the gentile before he touched it. And if you say that acquiring by pulling does not apply to a gentile, why is its money permitted? Rav Ashi replied: Here we are dealing with a case where he paid him a *zuz* in advance, before the measuring, and thereby acquired the wine with money.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:12.english: And they object: If that is so, that it refers to him paying in advance, say the last clause of the Mishna: 'If he measured before he fixed a price — its money is forbidden.' And if he paid him a *zuz* in advance, why is its money forbidden?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:13.english: Rav Ashi said to him: And according to your opinion, as you say that acquiring by pulling applies to a gentile, why in the first clause is its money permitted, and in the latter clause is its money forbidden?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:14.english: Rather, what do you have to say that you distinguish between the matters? That you say thus: When he fixes a price, his mind relies that the sale will not be canceled, and therefore the sale is concluded by pulling. But when he does not fix a price, his mind does not rely on it.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:15.english: According to my opinion as well, even though he paid him a *zuz* in advance, if he fixes a price for him, his mind relies on it. If he does not fix a price, his mind does not rely on it.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:16.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear another proof against your opinion, for Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: A descendant of Noah is executed for theft of less than the value of one *peruta*. However, for such a theft of less than one *peruta*, if he stole from a Jew — it is not subject to restitution; he is not obligated to return it to the Jew, since the Jew does not care about it. And if you say that acquiring by pulling does not apply to a gentile, why is the gentile executed? He did nothing by stealing an object, for the object remains the property of its original owner!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:17.english: And they respond: Because he caused the Jew distress by this taking, that he took property that was not his, even though from the perspective of the laws of acquisition, he did not acquire it.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:2.english: And they reject: If it is a case where the seller measures and pours it into the vessel of a Jew, it is indeed permitted to do so without receiving payment first. However, Rav's ruling is not necessary unless the gentile's vessel is set on the ground of the wine seller, and therefore it is not acquired by the gentile before it is rendered forbidden.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:3.english: And they object: Ultimately, even in this case, when the wine reaches the interior airspace of the vessel, the gentile acquires it, whereas it does not become wine used for a libation until it reaches the bottom of the vessel, and there is an acquisition here prior to the prohibition. Can one conclude from this that in the opinion of Rav a stream of liquid serves as a connection, and it is considered as if the forbidden wine at the bottom of the vessel and the wine being poured into it are connected?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:4.english: And they reject: No, a stream of liquid does not serve as a connection. Therefore, if the gentile is holding the vessel in his hand, the law is indeed that the acquisition occurs first and the money is permitted. However, Rav's ruling is not necessary unless the gentile's vessel is set on the ground of the wine seller, and therefore it is not acquired by the gentile before it is rendered forbidden.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:5.english: And they ask: Let the gentile's vessels acquire the wine for him when it reaches the interior airspace of the vessel! And if we do not say so, do you conclude from this a general *halakha* according to Rav, that if the buyer's vessels are in the seller's domain, the buyer does not acquire something that enters his vessels? And this matter is doubtful to the Sages, and remains in its source as an unresolved problem!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:6.english: And they reject: No, actually, I could say to you in general: The buyer acquires. And here, where the wine is rendered forbidden before being acquired by the gentile, what are we dealing with? For example, there is a remnant of wine on the mouth of the gentile's jug, which contains a little wine used for a libation, and therefore the wine poured into the jug is rendered forbidden, as each first bit that is poured becomes wine used for a libation because it mixes with the wine used for a libation found there. Therefore, Rav told the wine shopkeepers to take the payment for the wine before measuring it into the gentile's vessel.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:7.english: And they comment: And according to this explanation, in accordance with whose opinion did Rav say this? It is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel; for if it were in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, he says: That wine used for a libation that became mixed with other wine may all be sold to gentiles except for the value of the wine used for a libation that is in it. Therefore, it is permitted to take payment for the wine poured into the gentile's vessel, and we rule according to him!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:8.english: And they respond: The explanation of this *halakha* can be only according to Rav. For Rav says: The *halakha* is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel specifically when a barrel is mixed with a barrel, but not wine with wine, in which case all the wine is forbidden, including its monetary value. Thus, in any case, there is no proof from Rav's words that pulling does not acquire for a gentile.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:9.english: They raise another objection to Ameimar's words from what we learned: One who buys broken vessels from gentiles and finds idol worship among them, if he pulled the broken vessels before he gave zuzim to the gentile, he may return this idol worship, because he has not yet acquired it. If he pulled it after he gave zuzim, he must take this idol worship to the Dead Sea, for it is his, and he is obligated to destroy it. And now, if it enters your mind that acquiring by pulling applies to a gentile, as Ameimar says, why may he return it when he has pulled it? It is already his! Abaye said: Because it appears to be a mistaken transaction, for he certainly did not intend to buy idol worship.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 72a:1.english: And what is the meaning of 'it is not subject to restitution'? That it is not subject to the laws of restitution, for he did not actually steal the object.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 72a:2.english: And they object: If that is how you explain it, say the latter clause of this *halakha*: A gentile who stole from a Jew, and his friend, who is also a gentile, came and took it from him — he is executed for it. Granted, in the first clause, you explain that it is because he caused the Jew distress. But in the latter clause, what did the second one do?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 72a:3.english: Rather, conclude from it that acquiring by pulling applies to a gentile, and therefore the first one acquired the stolen item, and for this reason, the second one who stole it from him is also liable. And they conclude: Indeed, conclude from it that this is so.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:1.hebrew: ורמינהי עיר שכבשוה כרקום - וא"ת דלמא ההיא מיירי לאחר גמר המלחמה דאז יש להם פנאי? וי"ל דמשמע בכל ענין, אפי' קודם גמר המלחמה:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:1:1.english: And they raise a contradiction: A city that was conquered by a karkom - And if you ask: Perhaps that refers to after the war is over, when they have leisure? And it can be answered that it implies in any case, even before the war is over.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:4:1.hebrew: הא לא דמיא אלא לסיפא אבל אומר מלטני מן העוצר - פירש רש"י משום רבינו יחיאל: דכי אמר ליה הכי מותר, משום דמצי לסלוקי בזוזי מן העוצר, ואם כן כי נמי יהיב העובד כוכבים יין לעוצר לאו שליחות דישראל קא עביד, ומשום הכי שרי כי האי גוונא. אבל כי אמר ליה ״עול תחתי״, משמע הלשון: היה תחתי במקומי, וכל מה דיהיב כאילו יהיב ישראל דמי, דהא במקומו הוא, כפירשתי. ולי נראה: דאם כן פשיטא דמלטני מן העוצר דשרי, כיון דמיירי דיכול לסלקו. לכן נראה לי שהישראל חייב למלך יין (נסך), מכל מקום שרי כי אמר ליה ״מלטני מן העוצר״, משום דמשמע הכי קאמר ליה: סלק אותו במה שתוכל, אבל אינו מצווה לו לפרוע יין נסך, ולכך שרי אפילו לא מצי לסלוקי בזוזי אלא ביין נסך, ואפילו הקדים לו דינר. ואמר לעיל (עבודה זרה דף סג:) דאסור גבי פועלים, הכא שרי. דהתם היינו טעמא משום דהוא מקדים לו הדינר בשביל שיתן מיין נסך לפועלים, אבל הכא קאמר ליה שיסלקנו במעות אם יכול. הלכך לא חשיב כפורע יין מיין נסך. אבל כי אמר ליה ״עול תחתי״, הוי כמו שאמר ליה ״פרע למלך תחתי כמו שאני חייב לו יין״, ונמצא פורע חובו מיין נסך, ואפילו לא הקדים דינר אסור מטעם דפירשתי:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:6:1.hebrew: אמר אמימר משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה תדע דהני פרסאי משדרי פרדשני אהדדי ולא הדרי בהו - אומר רבי יצחק דאין זה עיקר הטעם אלא משום דאמימר סביר כר' יוחנן דאמר מעות קונות ודריש לעמיתך בכסף לעובד כוכבים במשיכה כדאמר בבכורות (דף יג: ושם) ומה שמביא ראיה מפרדשני דפרסאי אין זה כלום אלא אמתלא בעלמא שמנהג אבותיהם מן הפרסיים שאינם חוזרים אחר המשיכה שמע מינה שכך הדין:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:6:2.hebrew: פרדשני דורונות ולא הדרי בהו - אלמא קננהו במשיכה לאידך גיסא מתשובת הגאונים מי שיש לו כור חטים כו' פירש בקונטרס זה עיקר דלישנא קמא קני במתנה הוא והוא בא לומר דמשיכה קונה במקח וממכר ואומר רבי יצחק דאפילו למאן דאמר אינה קונה כרב אשי בסמוך הני מילי כגון דאיכא כספא אבל במציאה ומתנה דליכא כספא כולי עלמא מודו דקני במשיכה או בהגבהה:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:6:3.hebrew: רב אשי אמר משיכה בעובד כוכבים אינה קונה - לא לדיחויא בעלמא קאמר רב אשי הכי אלא לפי האמת כדמוכח במסכת בכורות פרק ב' (שם:) דקאמר רב אשי מדרישא משיכה אינה קונה סיפא נמי משיכה אינה קונה אלמא הכי סבירא ליה לרב אשי הלכך לא גרסינן במילתא דרב אשי לעולם אימא לך פירש רבינו תם דאף על גב דרב אשי בתרא הוה לית הלכתא כוותיה בהאי אלא קיימא לן כאמימר דאמר משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה דסבירא ליה כר' יוחנן כדפירשתי והלכה כרבי יוחנן לגבי רבי שמעון בן לקיש ופלוגתא היא דר' יוחנן פרק הזהב (ב"מ מז:) ר' יוחנן סבר מעות קונות דבר תורה ואם כן לדידיה דרשינן לעמיתך בכסף ולעובד כוכבים במשיכה ורבי שמעון בן לקיש סבר משיכה מפורשת מן התורה בישראל ואם כן דרשינן לעמיתך במשיכה ולעובד כוכבים בכסף והכי מוכח בבכורות והלכך משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה כר' יוחנן ואף על גב דרבא קאמר התם פרק הזהב קרא ומתניתין מסייע לרבי שמעון בן לקיש לא משום דסבירא ליה לרבא כרבי שמעון בן לקיש אבל מכל מקום לא קשיא לר' יוחנן דרבי יוחנן דחי להו שפיר כדפירשתי התם ותדע דהכי הוה כדפירשתי דלא משום דרבא סבר כרבי שמעון בן לקיש קאמר הכי שהרי רבא גופיה פוסק פרק החולץ (יבמות לו. ושם) כרבי שמעון בן לקיש לגבי ר' יוחנן בשלושה וחשיב להו התם אבל בעלמא בכל המקומות הלכה כר' יוחנן ואם היה סובר רבא כרבי שמעון בן לקיש בההיא דמשיכה מפורשת מן התורה אם כן הוה ליה למיחשביה התם וליכא למימר דלא חש למיחשביה משום דמתניתין מסייע ליה לרבי שמעון בן לקיש דהא בהני שלושה דקחשיב התם איכא דתניא כוותיה דרבי שמעון בן לקיש ואפילו הכי קחשיב לה התם אלא ודאי סבר כר' יוחנן בההיא דמעות קונות בישראל אם כן לעובד כוכבים במשיכה כדפירשתי אם כן המקנה בהמה לעובד כוכבים כדי לפוטרה מן הבכורה צריך שימשכנה העובד כוכבים ובכך סגי בלא כסף מיהו רש"י פירש דמשיכה אינה קונה בעובד כוכבים אלא כסף דאין הלכה כר' יוחנן אלא כרבי שמעון בן לקיש משום דרבא סבירא ליה כוותיה פרק הזהב מדקאמר קרא ומתניתין מסייע ליה לרבי שמעון בן לקיש וכי תימא אם כן אמאי לא חשיב לה בהחולץ בהדי הנהו שלושה צריך לומר משום דההיא דהזהב משיכה קונה קאמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש פרק שני בשמיה דר' אושעיא ובפרק החולץ אינו זוכר אלא הנהו דקאמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש משמיה דנפשיה דהכי נמי לא קא חשיב מילתא דישנה לשחיטה מתחילה ועד סוף דפרק השוחט (חולין דף כט:) משום דמשמיה דלוי סבא אמרה רבי שמעון בן לקיש והרוצה לחוש לדברי רש"י ורבינו תם המקנה בהמה לעובד כוכבים לפוטרה מן הבכורה צריך שיתן העובד כוכבים כסף וגם משיכת העובד כוכבים בסימטא או לרשותו של עובד כוכבים שהוא שלו ואם אין לו רשות לעובד כוכבים מקנה לו הישראל חדר בביתו והעובד כוכבים ינעול ויפתח דבהכי קני ליה לרשות כדאמר בגיטין פרק הזורק (גיטין דף עז:) ותיחוד ותפתח ואח"כ ימשוך העובד כוכבים הבהמה לאותו חדר ובבכורות פרק קמא (דף ג.) פליגי אמוראי מה צריך שיקנה העובד כוכבים מן הבהמה איכא מאן דאמר שצריך שיקנה דבר שעושה אותה טרפה ואיכא מאן דאמר אפילו אזנו ונראה להחמיר ולהקנות לעובד כוכבים דבר שעושה אותה טרפה כגון הריאה והראש מן הבהמה או מן העובר כשהיא מעוברת אמנם אין צריך שיתן העובד כוכבים מעות שוה הראש והריאה אלא סגי שיקנם בפרוטה ואף על פי ששוה יותר כפלים אף על פי כן אין לחוש משום ביטול מקח שאנן סהדי שהישראל גמר ואקני לעובד כוכבים כדי להפטר מן הבהמה:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71a:7:1.hebrew: שקילו זוזי מינייהו והדר כיילו להו וכולי ואי סלקא דעתך משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה מדמשכה עובד כוכבים קנייה וכולי לא צריכא דכייל ורמי למנא דעובד כוכבים - פירש אבל לעולם משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה כדפירשתי והקשה רבינו תם כיון דמשיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה אם כן מעות אינם קונות ואם כן מה היה מועיל המעות שהיו נותנים מתחלה מכל מקום הוי יין נסך ברשותו של ישראל מיד שנגע בו ועדיין אינו של עובד כוכבים עד שימשכנו כיון דמשיכה קונה ולא מעות ומיד שנגע בו העובד כוכבים נעשה יין נסך ברשות ישראל והמעות שביד ישראל נעשו למפרע דמי יין נסך ואין לומר שהעובדי כוכבים היו נותנין להם המעות במתנה דאטו בשופטני עסקינן ואומר רבי יצחק שבשעת נתינת הדמים היו אומרים להם העובדי כוכבים אנו מקנים לכם המעות מעכשיו והיין יהיה שלנו מעכשיו והעובדי כוכבים היו מאמינים אותם בטוב ולא היו יראים פן יגזלו ואף על פי שלא בא לידם עדיין או אי נמי יש לומר דסבר האי דדחייה דקונה משיכה או מעות בעובד כוכבים ודורש הכי לעמיתך במשיכה הא לעובד כוכבים או בהא או בהא ולית ליה הא דאמר בבכורות (דף יג.) מדה ישראל בחדא עובד כוכבים נמי בחדא ואם תאמר ולמה לא למדם להדיח כלי העובדי כוכבים או למדוד בכלי ישראל ויש לומר דבכך יש לטעות כמה פעמים אבל בלקיחת מעות קודם לא יבא לטעות כיון שהיה מנהגם כן:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:1.hebrew: בן נח נהרג על פחות משוה פרוטה - ובן נח מצווה על הגזל ואזהרתן זו מיתתן ולא ניתן להשבון ודוקא ישראל דבר מחילה הוא אבל עובד כוכבים לאו בר מחילה הוא ורש"י פירש דלא ניתן להשבון משום דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה ולא נראה דאם כן לא יתחייב עובד כוכבים לשלם גזלו בשום ענין:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:2.hebrew: ואי סלקא דעתך משיכה בעובד כוכבים אינה קונה אמאי נהרג - (פירש) הא לא קניה וכל היכא דאיתיה ברשותיה דישראל הוא וקשה דהא ישראל נמי לא קנה הגזילה להיות שלו ואף על פי כן קנייה להתחייב באונסין החיוב דשייך ביה והכי נמי יש לנו לומר בבן נח שקנאו להתחייב בה מיתה דהיינו החיוב דשייך בה ויש לומר דודאי. אי גזל שוה פרוטה דהוי ממונא לגבי ישראל וחיסרו אית לן למימר כדפירשתי אבל פחות משוה פרוטה שלא חיסר הישראל דלאו ממונא הוא וגם ממון העובד כוכבים לא נתרבה שהרי לא קנאה משום הכי פריך אמאי נהרג ומשני צערא דישראל [ועי' תוס' עירובין סב. ד"ה בן נח וכו' ביתר ביאור]:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:3:1.hebrew: שמע מינה נצוק חבור - ואם תאמר ולימא להו רב לסבוייתא ליקטפי קטופי ובכי האי גוונא שרי גם אי נצוק חבור כדקאמר לקמן (עבודה זרה דף עב:) ויש לומר לפי שהיו מוכרים יין הרבה היה להם טורח גדול לקטף:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:6:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן דאיכא עכבת יין אפומא דכוזנתא - תמיהא ליבטיל ההוא פורתא בשישים יש לומר דמין במינו הוא וקסבר דלא בטיל:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:8:1.hebrew: מידי הוא טעמא אלא לרב וכולי - ואם תאמר קשיא דרב אדרב דהכא מוקי אליבא דרב דמשיכה קונה בעובד כוכבים ובפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מח. ושם) משמע דסבירא ליה כרבי שמעון בן לקיש דמשיכה קונה בישראל ולא בעובד כוכבים גבי ההיא דמייתי התם נתנה לבלן ואמר רב עלה דוקא בלן דלא מיחסרא משיכה אבל ספר לא מעל עד דמשיך אלמא קסבר דמשיכה קונה בישראל אם כן אינה קונה בעובד כוכבים ומינה מסייע התם לרבי שמעון בן לקיש ואם כן קשה דרב אדרב מיהו יש ספרים דגרסי לעיל אמר רבא לסבוייתא אבל לא נראה מדאמר הכא מידי הוא טעמא אלא לרב האמר רב הלכה וכולי דעל כרחך היינו רב דאמר לקמן סוף פירקא הכי מדמייתי ר' יוחנן אבתריה ואם כן לעיל נמי בעובדא דסבוייתא גרסינן רב ולא רבא וקשה דרב אדרב ויש לומר דההוא דבלן מיירי לבלן עובד כוכבים ולכך קאמר רב דוקא בלן אבל ספר עובד כוכבים לא עד דמשיך דמשיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה כדאמר רב הכא והכי נמי צריך לאוקמי לרבי יוחנן דהתם כדפירשתי שם ותלמודא דמייתי נמי סייעתא לרבי שמעון בן לקיש התם פרק הזהב (שם) היינו לפי הפשט דמשמע דמיירי בישראל:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:9:1.hebrew: ואי סלקא דעתך משיכה בעובד כוכבים קונה אמאי יחזיר - ואם תאמר ואלא מאי מעות קונות אם כן אימא סיפא אם משנתן מעות משך יוליך הנאה לים המלח ולמה לי משך כיון דמעות קונות דכי האי גוונא פריך בבכורות (שם.) ואי סלקא דעתך מעות קונות למה לי משך ואם תאמר ומאי טעמא דמקשה דבעינן לומר שתיים ויש לומר משום דדורש לעמיתך בחדא במשיכה או בכסף לכל חד כדאית ליה ולעובד כוכבים עד דאיכא שתיים משיכה וכסף:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 72a:1:1.hebrew: ומאי לא ניתן להישבון - פירש דלא שייך ביה הישבון וכל היכא דאיתיה ברשותיה דישראל איתיה ותימה הרי ישראל נמי לא קנה הגזילה ואף על פי כן איתיה בתורת הישבון דכתיב והשיב הגזילה ונראה דהכי פירושו מאחר שאין חיוב בה רק משום צערא דישראל אמאי הוצרך לומר ולא ניתן להישבון פשיטא וליכא מאן דאמר שתהא השבה שייכא ביה ואם תאמר למאי דפירשנו לעיל דקאמר דמשיכה קונה בעובד כוכבים לכולי עלמא היכא דליכא זוזי כגון במציאה ובמתנה מאי פריך ומאי מייתי ראיה מגזל למקח וממכר ויש לומר דסבירא ליה דאי אינה קונה בעובד כוכבים במקח אף בגזל נמי לא תקנה דלא דמיא למציאה ומתנה דבהיתירא אתי לידיה אבל גזל דבאיסורא אתי לידיה אי לא מהני משיכה במקח לא מהני אף בגזל:
